questions.question: In the month of June, the number of girls in a class was half of the number of boys. In July, five more girls took admission, whereas five boys left the school. Now, the number of boys and girls is equal in the class. How many students in total were there in the class in June?
questions.solution:
Let the number of boys in a class in June = 2x

Then the number of girls in June = x

In July, the number of girls = x + 5

And the number of boys = 2x – 5

Now, according to the question, in July,

Number of girls = Number of boys

x + 5 = 2x – 5

→ x = 10

So, the number of boys in class in June = 2x = 2 × 10 = 20, and the number of girls in class in June = x = 10.

Hence, the total number of students is 20 + 10 = 30.

questions.question:
Select the number-pair in which the two numbers are related in the same way as are the two numbers of the following number-pair.

442 : 21
questions.solution:
The following logic is applied for 442 : 21

21² + 1 = 441 + 1 = 442

Similarly,

16² + 1 = 256 + 1 = 257

Hence, the correct answer is 257 : 16.

questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III.

Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) follow the statements.

**Statements:**

All parks are schools.

No school is a college.

**Conclusions:**

I. No college is a school.

II. Some schools are parks.

III. No park is a college.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow.
Only conclusion I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow.

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/256f5999c5e8a10040d41cd03eef4df262891d2f32bbc1c131c78284bf6ee307.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. No college is a school → True (No school is college.)

II. Some schools are parks → True (All parks are schools)

III. No park is a college → True (All parks are schools and no school is college so no park will be college)

Hence, the correct answer is ‘All the conclusions follow’.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(4, 6, 52)
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

(4, 6, 52) → 4² + 6² = 16 + 36 = 52

Similarly,

(3, 5, 34) → 3² + 5² = 9 + 25 = 34

Hence, the correct answer is (3, 5, 34).
